## Source 1 — World Economic Forum Future of Jobs Report 2025: "40% of employers expect to reduce workforce where AI can automate tasks"

**Type:** Academic / policy research (WEF, cited in Daily News Tanzania + multiple secondary sources)
**Engagement signal:** Very high — the "40% will reduce workforce" stat is the new anchor (replacing the older "47% jobs at risk" Oxford 2013 stat)
**Headline:** "Will AI Replace Our Work? Insights From Shanghai Forum 2026" / Journalism-AI intersection coverage

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "In February 2025, the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report reveals that 40% of employers expect to reduce their workforce where AI can automate tasks."

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- "AI will kill journalism / my industry" — the doom frame
- "40% of employers" — the specific number the audience will quote back
- "co-pilot" — the optimistic frame (sift through data, catch errors)
- "AI is reshaping how labor would be defined, organized, and valued" — the Fudan Shanghai Forum frame (structural transformation, not displacement)

### Why this works:
The 40% stat is the new load-bearing number. The 2013 Oxford "47% at risk" stat is now 12 years old and dated; the 2025 WEF "40% will reduce workforce where AI can automate" is the current generation's anchor. The Pillar 5 angle: "40% of employers plan to reduce headcount where AI can automate. That's not 'AI takes your job' — it's 'the employer wants to spend $2K/month on AI instead of $5K/month on you.' The lever is being the one who uses the AI, not the one who competes against it." The voice: stats → implication → 30-minute action.

## Source 2 — 网易: "2026年,AI正在这样改变你的工作方式" — AI takes the repetitive, you take the judgment

**Type:** Chinese tech-news piece (m.163.com)
**Engagement signal:** High — the 2026 work-change framing
**Headline:** "2026年AI正在这样改变你的工作方式"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "你有没有发现,身边的同事越来越少提'加班'这个词了?不是工作变少了,是AI把重复性任务接了过去。2026年的职场,写周报、整理数据、排会议这些琐事,正在被自动化工具批量处理。你省下的时间,被迫拿去处理更复杂的人际协调和创意决策。"
> "工具越智能,对'人'的要求反而更刁钻。以前会用Excel就能混的岗位,现在需要你同时懂业务逻辑、会调教AI、还能在机器给出的十个方案里挑出真正靠谱的那个。"

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- "AI把重复性任务接了过去" (AI took the repetitive tasks) — the relief
- "被迫拿去处理更复杂的人际协调" (forced to handle more complex coordination) — the new demand
- "对'人'的要求反而更刁钻" (the demands on the human are now MORE specific) — the new bar
- "AI协调员" (AI coordinator) — the new role emerging
- "以前会用Excel就能混的岗位" (the old "Excel is enough" job) — the disappearing role

### Why this works:
The "对'人'的要求反而更刁钻" line is the load-bearing reframing. The doom version is "AI takes your job." The leverage version is "AI takes the easy parts of your job and makes the hard parts the only thing left." The audience doesn't get fired; they get promoted past the grunt work, OR they fall behind because they can't do the new hard part. The Pillar 5 angle: "The 30 minutes this weekend isn't about learning AI. It's about being the person who can do the new hard part (judgment + coordination) instead of being the person who only does the part that just got automated." The voice: X is gone → Y is the new thing → here's the 30-min tactical play.

## Source 3 — 李彦宏 (Baidu CEO) at WAIC 2024: "AI替代的是脑力劳动的体力活"

**Type:** Public speech, quoted in Sohu + mobile-Sohu
**Engagement signal:** High — 李彦宏 is the most-quoted Chinese AI executive on this framing
**Headline:** "专家:AI替换的是脑力劳动的体力活"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "AI将替代脑力劳动的体力活?专家对此给出了他的看法。在2024世界人工智能大会上,百度创始人李彦宏表示,AI目前更多是辅助人工作,而不是替代人。他指出,AI技术的发展已经催生了一些全新的工作机会,如数据标注师和提示词工程师等。"
> "AI更多的是替代那些脑力劳动的体力活。例如,在处理大量数据和复杂分析时,AI可以帮助人类更高效地完成任务,但决策和创新等高层次的脑力劳动仍然需要人类的智慧和判断。"

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- "脑力劳动的体力活" (the physical labor of mental work) — the new distinction
- "数据标注师和提示词工程师" (data labelers and prompt engineers) — the new roles
- "决策和创新等高层次的脑力劳动" (decision-making and innovation) — the part AI doesn't replace
- "金手指和金头脑" (golden hands and golden minds) — the 熊辉 parallel frame

### Why this works:
The "脑力劳动的体力活" framing is the cleanest version of the leverage play. The persona's Example 6 ("The goal of automation isn't to fire your staff. It's to take the robot out of the human.") is the English-language parallel. The Pillar 5 angle: "Your weekly report is the 体力活 of 脑力劳动. The boss doesn't read it; they skim it. That's the 体力活. The decision on what to put in it, what to cut, what to flag — that's the 脑力劳动. AI does the 体力活. You do the 脑力劳动. That's the leverage." The voice: bilingual X→Y pivot.

## Source 4 — 知乎: "AI和机器人并不影响你的工作(job),它们影响的是任务(task)"

**Type:** Chinese practitioner post (zhuanlan.zhihu.com)
**Headline:** "工作的重新定义"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "AI和机器人并不影响我们的工作(job),它们影响的是任务(task)。工作拆解成不同任务后,公司需要判断哪些任务适合于自动化、适合于哪些类型的自动化;再将余下的工作重新构建成高价值的工作,交给具备相关技能的人去完成,以让他们发挥出自身的最大价值。"

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- "工作 vs 任务" (job vs task) — the reframe
- "高价值的工作" (high-value work) — the new role
- "重新构建" (rebuild) — the structural frame

### Why this works:
The job-vs-task distinction is the cleanest leverage frame. The persona's voice: "Your job isn't going away. The 12 tasks that make up your job — 4 of them are about to be automated. The other 8 are about to be worth more." The Pillar 5 angle: the 30-min weekend task isn't "learn AI" — it's "look at your job description, list 12 tasks, mark the 4 that are about to be automated, become the person who's undeniable on the other 8."
